title: GlossEntry
description:
A prebuilt gloss for one frequent word form (§18), shown in the word
popover and used by lessons. Keyed by surface form, because that is what
the Reader looks up; `lemma`/`root`/`affixes` give the breakdown.

affixes.description: Display breakdown in order, e.g. `["meN-", "baca"]` or `["ke-", "sehat", "-an"]`.

arabic_origin.description:
The Arabic source word when this is an Arabic loan; the full card lives
in the Arabic Bridge dataset under the same `word`.

false_friend.description:
Loud warning when the word looks like an Arabic word but means
something else (kalimat ≠ «كلمة»).

indonesian.description:
Javanese only: the Indonesian equivalent, since the learner meets
Javanese after BIPA 1 and compares the two.

lemma.description: Dictionary headword (equals `word` for bare roots and particles).

note.description: Usage or register note worth knowing (optional).

rank.description: Rank in the frequency list (1 = most frequent).

root.description: Morphological root when the word is derived (membaca → baca).

speech_level.description:
Javanese only: the speech level of this form; its equivalents at the
other levels live in the speech-level table.

word.description: Surface form, lowercase, as in the frequency list.

Example.description: An example sentence with its translations.

sense.description: Index into `senses` of the meaning this example shows.

text.description: The sentence in the learning language. Contains the word (or a form of it).

Pos.description: Part of speech, coarse enough for exercises and popovers.

Provenance.description: Who produced a piece of content, so a better pass can replace it later.

prompt.description: Versioned prompt id, e.g. `gloss@v1`. Empty for imports.

Register.description: Register of a word or sense.

ReviewStatus.description:
Whether the learner has reviewed an item. Everything starts unverified;
Javanese stays unverified until the learner (or a native speaker) approves it.

oneOf.description: Reviewed and found wrong; kept so the next batch regenerates it.

gloss.description: Short gloss in each voice (a few words, not a definition essay).

oneOf.description: Plain speech: friends, younger people, yourself.
The in-between level used in markets and casual polite talk.
Polite speech to elders, strangers, people of higher status.
Honorific words that elevate the other person (their body, actions, belongings).
Humble words for your own actions toward a respected person.

Trilingual.description: The same text in the three explanation voices (§11).
